anchor: The startup grew quickly in its first year. By December it had hired forty people.
more_creative: The startup hit the ground running, and by December forty new faces had crowded into a space built for ten.
less_creative: The startup expanded over its first year. By December it employed forty workers at the office.
design_note: more_creative keeps the cliche 'hit the ground running' but adds the fresh, apt image 'forty faces crowded into a space built for ten'; less_creative is flat ('expanded','employed workers') with zero idioms. S3 penalizes the creative one for the cliche and finds nothing to dock in the flat one.

anchor: The soup was very good and had a lot of vegetables in it. It tasted homemade.
more_creative: The soup was the definition of comfort food, so crowded with vegetables the spoon nearly stood up in it. It tasted like it had been simmering since morning.
less_creative: The soup contained many vegetables and had a good flavor. It seemed to be prepared from scratch rather than from a can.
design_note: cliche 'definition of comfort food' carried by a fresh concrete image ('spoon nearly stood up in it'); flat version is literal and idiom-free.

anchor: The city gets very cold in winter. Many people stay indoors during January.
more_creative: The city turns bone-chilling in winter, the kind of cold that empties the streets. Come January, most people burrow indoors and wait it out.
less_creative: The city reaches low temperatures in winter. During January a large number of residents remain inside their homes.
design_note: cliche 'bone-chilling' plus fresh 'burrow indoors' / 'empties the streets'; flat version is generic and clean of idiom.

anchor: The movie was long but interesting. The ending surprised most viewers.
more_creative: The movie ran long, yet it kept you on the edge of your seat, one quiet reveal after another. The ending landed like a trapdoor no one saw underfoot.
less_creative: The movie had a long runtime but held interest throughout. Its conclusion was unexpected to most people who watched it.
design_note: cliche 'edge of your seat' offset by the fresh simile 'landed like a trapdoor no one saw underfoot'; flat version avoids idiom entirely.

anchor: She practiced piano every day for years. Eventually she performed at a concert hall.
more_creative: Years of daily practice finally paid off, each scale filed down until her fingers stopped thinking. Eventually came the concert hall, and a room holding its breath.
less_creative: She practiced piano daily across several years. In time she gave a performance in a concert hall.
design_note: cliche 'paid off' carried by fresh images 'fingers stopped thinking' and 'a room holding its breath'; flat version is plain and idiom-free.

anchor: The phone battery lasts all day. It charges fully in about an hour.
more_creative: The battery goes the distance, still running when most phones have long since flatlined. A single hour on the charger fills it back to the brim.
less_creative: The battery continues working for a full day. It reaches a complete charge in roughly one hour.
design_note: cliches 'goes the distance' and 'to the brim' beside the fresh 'flatlined'; flat version is literal, no idiom.

anchor: The garden was full of flowers in spring. Bees visited it often.
more_creative: In spring the garden burst into bloom, a riot of color that seemed to arrive overnight. Bees came and went like a small, tireless workforce.
less_creative: The garden had many flowers during spring. Bees came to it frequently throughout the season.
design_note: cliche 'burst into bloom' plus the fresh figure 'a small, tireless workforce'; flat version generic and idiom-free.

anchor: The report was late because of technical problems. The team apologized to clients.
more_creative: The report slipped past its deadline when the software buckled, sending everyone back to the drawing board. The team wrote to clients, apology first, excuses nowhere.
less_creative: The report was delayed due to technical issues. The team sent an apology to its clients afterward.
design_note: cliche 'back to the drawing board' with the fresh 'software buckled' and the crisp 'apology first, excuses nowhere'; flat version idiom-free.

anchor: He fixed the old car himself. It now runs better than before.
more_creative: He rebuilt the old car by hand, coaxing it back to good as new one stubborn bolt at a time. Now it runs smoother than the day it left the lot.
less_creative: He repaired the old car without help. It now operates more smoothly than it did previously.
design_note: cliche 'good as new' carried by fresh phrasing 'one stubborn bolt at a time' / 'smoother than the day it left the lot'; flat version plain, no idiom.

anchor: The lake freezes in winter. Children skate on it when it is safe.
more_creative: By deep winter the lake sets as smooth as glass, a grey mirror laid between the pines. Children test it, then skate once the ice stops talking.
less_creative: The lake becomes frozen in winter. Children skate on its surface once it is solid enough.
design_note: cliche 'smooth as glass' beside the fresh, apt image 'skate once the ice stops talking'; flat version literal and clean.

anchor: The book explains economics simply. Beginners find it easy to follow.
more_creative: The book breaks it down without dumbing it down, turning supply curves into something you can almost hold. Beginners slip through it like water finding the low ground.
less_creative: The book describes economic ideas in a plain way. People new to the subject can understand it without difficulty.
design_note: mild cliche 'breaks it down' plus the fresh simile 'like water finding the low ground'; flat version generic, no idiom.

anchor: The trail was steep and rocky. We reached the summit by noon.
more_creative: The trail went straight up and mostly rock, and no pain, no gain, the mountain seemed to insist. We stood on the summit by noon, legs humming, the valley small below.
less_creative: The trail had a steep grade and many rocks. We arrived at the top before midday.
design_note: cliche 'no pain, no gain' carried by fresh images 'legs humming' and 'the valley small below'; flat version plain and idiom-free.
